title: The image moves farther away
hook: Change image distance and predict magnification magnitude.

doesNotKnow: magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance

misconception: magnification magnitude stays fixed when image distance doubles.
objective: Apply magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance to compare magnification magnitude when image distance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With thin-lens configurations with fixed object distance and refocusing lenses of different focal lengths, magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance. When image distance doubles, magnification magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider thin-lens configurations with fixed object distance and refocusing lenses of different focal lengths, with a nonzero initial result. If image distance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on magnification magnitude?
recall.why: Apply magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
